ownership_reason: Only the gold forms the product and decides whether it fits in a long; hop 1 orders the two factors (smaller first, the original's symmetry step) and hops 2-4 pass them on, each receiving a long back. Long.MIN_VALUE is also the correct product of (Long.MIN_VALUE, 1) and of (Long.MIN_VALUE / 2, 2), both asserted by the trigger, so no caller can tell the wrapped product of (Long.MIN_VALUE, -1) from a valid one. Hops 2-5 document the ordering they receive (first factor not greater than the second), so the pair always reaches the gold as (Long.MIN_VALUE, -1); passing it the other way round breaks that documented ordering. The gold's javadoc promises an ArithmeticException when the result can not be represented as a long, which 2^63 cannot. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the facade's javadoc; MathUtils.subAndCheck(long, long) treats a subtrahend of Long.MIN_VALUE as its own case because its negation wraps (testSubAndCheckLong: subAndCheck(0L, Long.MIN_VALUE) throws); MathUtils.lcm(long, long) rejects a result whose absolute value wraps to Long.MIN_VALUE, i.e. 2^63 (testLcmLong: lcm(Long.MIN_VALUE, 1) throws); the int overload mulAndCheck(int, int) widens the product and rejects anything outside the int range, Integer.MIN_VALUE * -1 included (testMulAndCheck).
